newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL says weak NZ economy hits ad volumes.
newsitem.headline: INL says weak NZ economy hits ad volumes.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Ltd said on Friday the weak New Zealand economy had hit advertising volumes at the start of the 1998 year, but it was confident net profit could be increased this financial year.
INL reported a net profit of NZ$50.42 million for the year to June 30 1997, up from $47.18 million a year earlier.
"A weakening New Zealand economy has had an impact on advertising volumes at the start of the 1998 financial year.
"However, the company is benefiting from a more efficient cost structure and remains confident that net profit can be increased this financial year," INL said in a statement.
Chairman Colin Maiden said the 1997/98 result was most satisfactory considering the difficult trading environment which had prevailed through much of the year.
Tax paid profit of $50.42 million after goodwill and unusual or non-trading items was 6.9 percent ahead of last year and also a record for the company, he said.
Profit after tax but before abnormals and goodwill was $60.03 million.

Major non-trading or unusual items included a restructuring of the company's Gordon and Gotch magazine distribution operations in Australia, an accounting adjustment relating to previous years' earnings from Gordon and Gotch in New Zealand, a one-off write-down of subsidiary Terabyte's CD-Rom publishing venture Teramedia in the United States, and various restructuring expenses in New Zealand, the company said.

"The year's trading was characterised by a strong performance on the part of the company's New Zealand operations and a greatly improved second half from Gordon and Gotch Australia following restructuring.
Printing and publishing revenues rose by 1.3 percent and magazine distribution gross billings by 5.7 percent.
Overall, sales rose by 3.6 percent to $953.9 million.

"Although total newspaper advertising volumes in New Zealand were 3.3 percent lower than the previous year, newsprint cost savings and tight control of other expenses saw all New Zealand divisions deliver improved earnings compared with the previous year," INL said.

Newspaper circulations were generally held, although The Dominion in Wellington, Tha Waikato Times and Sunday News all made worthwhile gains. In magazine publishing, strong circulation gains were posted by New Zeaalnd Gardener and New Zealand House and Garden.

"The strength displayed by the company's Auckland operations was a feature of the result. The group now has six divisions based in Auckland producing collective earnings well in excess of any other region," INL said.

"News Media (Auckland) saw a further improvement in advertising volumes and yields in the Sunday Star-Times while TV guide circulation held up well in the face of new competition in the Auckland market."
Net debt (after $76 million of cash or cash equivalents) stood at $28 million at June 30, a reduction of $38 million during the year.
INL declared a final dividend for the year of 12 cents per share, bringing the total dividend for the year to 23 cents per share against last year's 22 cents.
INL is 49.5 percent owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp.
